title: Track overload-protected errors separately from internal 5xx for error budget accounting
author: Aisha Bello
description: Context: As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding, we’re intentionally returning customer-actionable overload responses (429/503 with Redwood overload codes + Retry-After) to protect the platform. Those requests should not be counted as “internal server errors” for error budget burn, otherwise we page/penalize teams during intentional shedding and can’t distinguish true regressions from overload protection working as designed. This PR extends slo-toolkit’s event model and burn calculators to classify errors into (a) internal failures vs (b) overload-protected responses, and to surface both series in SLO outputs so alerting can be aligned to the new policy. Summary of changes: 1) Adds an explicit failure_class dimension: internal | overload_protected | client (existing behavior was effectively internal vs non-internal based on status class). 2) Updates the HTTP status + error-code mapping used by slo-toolkit to recognize Redwood overload-protected responses (e.g., 429/503 paired with Redwood overload codes) as overload_protected, not internal. 3) Updates burn-rate and error budget accounting to compute internal_error_ratio and overload_shed_ratio separately. By default, only internal_error_ratio contributes to budget burn; overload_shed_ratio is emitted and can be alerted on independently (optional). 4) Adds backward-compatible config flag: slo.failure_classification.v2=true to enable classification by Redwood error codes when present, otherwise fallback to status-based rules (to avoid breaking older agents). 5) Adds tests and a small migration note for dashboards/alerts expecting the previous “5xx ratio” series name. Why this approach: We want to preserve a strict definition of “platform reliability” while also measuring and controlling customer impact from shedding. Separating the series enables: (a) paging on internal failures without flapping during expected overload, and (b) a dedicated alert when overload shedding is unusually high/continuous (i.e., capacity shortfall). Notes: This does not change ingestion; it only changes classification + SLO computations at query/runtime. The Redwood-specific mapping is keyed off error_code in the standard error envelope (and for OpenAI-compat, off error.type where we map Redwood overload codes into a stable shape). Follow-ups: redwood/observability-pack will update default dashboards to show both ratios side-by-side and to update the “availability” panels to use internal_error_ratio. See ENG-4830/ENG-4840.
commits: slo: add failure_class to request outcome model
slo: classify overload-protected errors via status+redwood error codes
slo: split budget burn into internal_error_ratio vs overload_shed_ratio
config: add v2 classification flag + defaults
tests: fixtures for 429/503 overload envelopes + OpenAI-compat mapping
docs: migration note for consumers of legacy 5xx ratio series
review_conversation: Sergio Costa: Can we confirm these overload-protected responses won’t burn the main availability SLO? We should still be able to alert if shedding is elevated for too long.

Aisha Bello (author): Yes. internal_error_ratio is now the default burn input; overload_shed_ratio is emitted as a separate series. We can wire an alert on sustained overload_shed_ratio > X% in a follow-up (ENG-4840).
Allison Grant: Please be careful about label/cardinality. Are we adding new labels to the emitted series?

Aisha Bello (author): No new high-cardinality labels. failure_class is a bounded enum (3 values). We also kept existing route/model/region labeling unchanged; classification is computed per stream, not increasing dimensions beyond one bounded label.
Tomáš Novák: How does this interact with older agents that don’t attach Redwood error_code? We don’t want silent misclassification.

Aisha Bello (author): Guarded behind slo.failure_classification.v2=true. If v2 enabled but error_code missing, we fall back to status-based rules (5xx => internal, 429 => client). For 503, we only mark overload_protected when error_code indicates overload; otherwise stays internal.
Christine Wong: For OpenAI-compat endpoints we map overload codes into error.type. Are we handling both error_code and error.type?
Aisha Bello (author): Yes—classifier checks (1) redwood.error_code if present, else (2) openai.error.type for the mapped overload types. Added fixtures for both shapes.
Sergio Costa: Requested change: rename series keys to be explicit (avoid ‘shed_rate’ vs ‘overload’ ambiguity) and add a short migration note.
Aisha Bello (author): Done. Series keys are now internal_error_ratio and overload_shed_ratio; added docs/migrations/2025-12-overload-protected-series.md and a changelog entry.
Allison Grant: Approved after the series rename + migration doc. Thanks.
Tomáš Novák: Approved. This will make incident reporting much cleaner.
Christine Wong: Approved. Matches ADR direction for overload taxonomy + SLO accounting.
release_notes: SLO toolkit now emits separate series for internal failures vs overload-protected responses. Error budget burn uses internal_error_ratio by default; overload_shed_ratio is available for dashboards/alerts. Enable Redwood-aware classification via slo.failure_classification.v2=true.
